title: Diamond Cut Definition
description: A structured, sourced definition of a diamond cut, including trade-name cuts that grading laboratories describe by geometry rather than by name.

name.description: The common name of the cut.

aliases.description: Other names the cut is sold or searched under.

trade_name.description: True if the name is a trade name rather than an officially recognized gemological shape.

officially_recognized_shape.description: True only if a major grading laboratory recognizes this exact name as an official shape. For trade names this is false.

certificate_term.description: How a grading report most often describes the geometry.

definition.description: The canonical one-sentence, plain-English definition of the cut.

outline.description: The face-up outline of the finished stone.

end_treatment.description: How the ends of the stone are finished (for example angular points along the long edges tapering toward each end, or pointed with French tips).

faceting_pattern.description: The faceting style of the stone.

faceting_status.description: Free-text status note used when the faceting pattern is pending confirmation.

typical_min.description: Lower end of the typical market range.

typical_max.description: Upper end of the typical market range.

recommended_min.description: Lower end of the maintainer's recommended cutting range.

recommended_max.description: Upper end of the maintainer's recommended cutting range.

units.description: Dimensionless ratio of length to width in millimeters.

durability_notes.description: Plain notes on chip resistance and wear.

inclusion_visibility.description: Whether the faceting pattern tends to hide, not affect, or reveal inclusions.

published_by.description: Who publishes this plain, repeatable definition.

claim_scope.description: Exactly what is claimed. We publish this definition and cut these stones in-house. Stay narrow and true.

claim_boundary.description: What is explicitly NOT claimed (for example invention, patent, or trademark).

sources.description: One entry per measurable or contestable claim. Every pricing or market claim must carry a source and a date.

updated.description: Date this record was last updated.
